# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.
data.title: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Goal

Make the stored **Teleport** power-up activate **automatically**, the same way **Phase Shift** already does, instead of requiring a manual **S / ↓** key press. This removes the S / ↓ key conflict that blocks the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG) and frees S / ↓ for held reverse thrust.

## User story

As a player, when a hostile threat closes in and I hold a stored Teleport, I want the teleport to fire automatically (like Phase Shift) so I am not required to reach for a key in the middle of dodging — and so movement keys are never overloaded with a consumable ability.

## Background / existing state

- **Phase Shift already auto-triggers** through the shared, single code path: `CombatScene._updatePhaseShiftAutoTrigger(dt)` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) calls the pure `isInDanger(player, bodies, bullets)` helper (`src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`; danger when the combined hostile-threat count within `DANGER_RADIUS` is >= 3) and feeds the result to `EffectsRegistry.updateDanger(inDanger, dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`). The registry handles charge availability, re-arm-on-danger-cleared and a post-trigger cooldown, and plays the Phase Shift cue on activation. Every combat scene (game + gyms) calls this once per frame.
- **Teleport is manual:** `CombatScene._handleTeleport()` fires on `JustDown(teleportKey)` or the hardcoded ↓ fallback and calls `triggerTeleport()`, which consumes one stored Teleport stack (FIFO) and warps the player to the nearest safe spot along the heading, granting Phase Shift on arrival. Documented in GDD §4.4 / controls table as **S / ↓**.

## Expected behaviour

- Teleport auto-activates when the player is **in danger** (same danger definition/feed as Phase Shift) **and** a stored Teleport charge exists **and** the re-arm conditions are met (danger cleared since last trigger, cooldown elapsed) — mirroring the Phase Shift auto-trigger contract.
- Manual S / ↓ activation is **removed**; S / ↓ becomes available for the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG).
- Teleport keeps its existing trigger path: nearest safe spot in the direction of travel, consuming one FIFO stack, granting Phase Shift on arrival, and the existing Phase Shift activation cue plays.
- One shared implementation in the combat core so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — to be finalised by this item's own intake)

1. Teleport auto-activates via the shared danger feed when the ship is in danger, a Teleport stack is available, and the re-arm conditions (danger cleared + cooldown) are satisfied.
2. No manual S / ↓ (or `layerDrop`) activation of Teleport remains in the game or gyms; the ↓ fallback key is removed.
3. A stored Teleport is consumed exactly once per activation; stacking/FIFO semantics are unchanged.
4. The trigger uses the existing safe-spot + Phase Shift-on-arrival path; game and gyms share one implementation (gym↔game parity).
5. The re-arm/cooldown behaviour matches the documented Phase Shift model.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD controls table, §4.4, any UI/HUD hints, code comments) — including the removal of S / ↓ for teleport.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes, with new/updated tests covering the auto-trigger, re-arm, and no-manual-key contracts.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — replace `_handleTeleport`/`teleportKey`/`downKey` with an automatic trigger fed by the shared danger feed.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add Teleport auto-trigger state (charge check, re-arm, cooldown) alongside the Phase Shift model.
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` — reused as-is (shared danger signal).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/*` — remove manual key wiring; ensure the shared auto-trigger runs.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the controls table and §4.4.
- Tests: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/RebindableControls.test.ts`.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-teleport may fire more often than a player wants (each stored teleport is precious). Mitigation: match the Phase Shift re-arm/cooldown contract and make the trigger threshold explicit and testable.
- **Assumption:** "like Phase Shift" means the same danger-based auto-trigger model (not a timer), and the manual binding is removed entirely.
- **Blocker for:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG (reverse thruster on S / ↓).
data.title: Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust)

# Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss to require 200 hits total (readable as 4 phases of 50) and I want its health bar pinned to the top of the screen so I can always read my progress regardless of where the boss is.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC1 and AC4.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` and `_totalHp = BOSS_PHASE_COUNT * BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` (400 total). Doc comment and `BossConfig.initialHp` comment reference 400/100.
- `healthBarGraphics` is created with `scene.add.graphics()`, then `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` puts it in the boss **container**, so it renders offset by the boss position even though `_drawHealthBar()` uses screen coordinates and `setScrollFactor(0)`.
- `getHpFraction()` is already proportional and the four phase-segment dividers already exist — keep both.

## Desired change

1. Change `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` to `50`; total becomes **200**. Update every comment/constant reference from 100/400 to 50/200 (including `BossConfig.initialHp` docs).
2. Remove the `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` container membership so the bar is a **scene child** (it is already created via `scene.add.graphics()`); keep `setScrollFactor(0)` and `setDepth(100)`. It now renders at the absolute screen coordinates drawn by `_drawHealthBar()` (horizontally centred at `BOSS_HEALTH_BAR_Y`).
3. Keep the proportional fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
4. Ensure `destroy()` still explicitly destroys `healthBarGraphics`.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — HP constants/comments, health-bar re-parenting.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — health-model and health-bar placement tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym health-bar placement expectations.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — health-bar layering assumptions if any.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE === 50` and total HP is 200; hitting 49 times keeps phase 1, the 50th hit advances to phase 2, and the 200th hit destroys the boss.
- The health bar Graphics is **not** a child of the boss container and its screen position is unchanged when the boss position changes (assert `boss.x`/`boss.y` separately from the bar's drawn position).
- `getHpFraction()` decreases monotonically with each hit from 1.0 toward 0.
- The four phase-segment dividers and the proportional fill are retained.
- All `Boss.test.ts` / `GymBoss.test.ts` assertions updated for 200 HP pass.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC1) **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- (parent AC4) **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
data.title: Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

# Increase per-phase boss minion counts

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss reinforced by more minions so the fight feels dangerous; as a developer I want the counts defined once in the shared minion planner.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC2.

## Existing state

- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` `BOSS_MINION_WAVES`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `minionCountForPhase(phase)` derives counts from `wavePlannedSpawnCount(wave.groups)`.

## Desired change

Retune to P1 = **12 scouts (6 per side)**, P2 = **12 divers (6 per side)**, P3 = **0**, P4 = **15 swarm**. Keep formations, keys, shootEnabled flags and phase-3 emptiness unchanged.

## Key Files

- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — group counts/positions.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts` — per-phase count assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym minion-count expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `minionCountForPhase(1) === 12`, `=== 12` for phase 2, `=== 0` for phase 3, `=== 15` for phase 4.
- `planMinionSpawns(phase).length` matches `minionCountForPhase(phase)` for every phase.
- Phase 1 and phase 2 are split into two groups of 6; phase 4 is a single group of 15.
- Existing shootEnabled semantics per phase are unchanged.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC2) **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
data.title: Increase per-phase boss minion counts

# Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want a distinct, punchy sound on every boss hit so hits feel responsive and obviously register.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the SFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes the boss cues (`playBossFireSound`, etc.) via the shared ToneForge playback layer.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps every sound-producing cue to a recipe (baked/existing-recipe/runtime-shim) and seeds; `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` is the typed runtime view; `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` enforces completeness.
- Baked WAVs live in `public/audio/sfx/` and are **tracked in git**; recipes live in `audio/toneforge/recipes/`.

## Desired change

1. Add a new recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` producing a short, punchy boss-hit impact (model the YAML shape on `aihell-boss-fire.yaml`).
2. Add a new baked manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`: `{ "cue": "playBossHitSound", "recipe": "aihell-boss-hit", "delivery": "baked", "seeds": [<new seed>] }`.
3. Add `playBossHitSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (delegating to `playCue`).
4. Render and commit the baked WAV `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` via the documented audio build pipeline (`scripts/build-audio.sh` / ToneForge).
5. Add/extend the cue-manifest contract test to require `playBossHitSound`.

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` (new).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue entry + seed.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` (new, committed).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playBossHitSound()`.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` — mapping/contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `playBossHitSound` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and appears in `CUE_MANIFEST` with recipe `aihell-boss-hit` and delivery `baked`.
- The recipe YAML exists, is valid, and the baked WAV for its seed is present under `public/audio/sfx/` and tracked.
- The cue-manifest contract test passes and fails if `playBossHitSound` is removed.
- No new runtime dependency is added.
data.title: Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue
